New York-based registered dietitian Kelly Springer shares research on highly processed foods and explains how combining fruits, vegetables, nuts and other nutrient-rich options can support long-term health. Eating just two slices of deli meat a day was associated with a substantially higher risk of dementia, according to a new review of ultra-processed foods (UPFs) and brain health. The findings, published in the August 2026 issue of Annual Review of Nutrition, looked at dozens of human and animal studies, including one involving nearly 500,000 people in the U.K. The study found that each additional 25 grams of processed meat eaten daily corresponded with a 44% higher risk of all-cause dementia and a 52% higher risk of Alzheimer's. Twenty-five grams of processed meat equals roughly one to two slices of deli meat, depending on how thick the meat is sliced. items.text: 5 Vital Health Markers In Your Lab Report You Should Know About
items.article: From checking blood sugar to looking for signs of inflammation, lab reports provide useful clues about what is happening inside your body. A blood test can tell you much more about your health than you may realise. From checking blood sugar to looking for signs of inflammation, lab reports provide useful clues about what is happening inside your body. But with so many numbers and medical terms on a report, it can be difficult to know which results deserve attention. Nutritionist Nmami Agarwal highlights five health markers that people may want to understand when looking at their reports. These include HbA1c, LDL and triglycerides, ferritin, fasting insulin and HOMA-IR, and hs-CRP. On Instagram, Agarwal explains that HbA1c shows the average blood sugar level over the past three months, rather than showing only one day's reading. LDL and triglycerides are part of a cholesterol test. LDL is one type of cholesterol, while triglycerides are a type of fat in the blood. Their levels can provide information about how the body handles fats and extra calories. Ferritin tells you about the iron stored in the body. A low ferritin level can mean that your iron stores are low, even if your hemoglobin looks normal. Fasting insulin and HOMA-IR can provide information about how the body uses insulin and may help identify insulin resistance early. items.article: Lal Bahadur Shastri’s life and politics were deeply influenced by Mahatma Gandhi, from the freedom movement to the Tashkent agreement of 1966. It’s a matter of coincidence that two of India’s greatest leaders in the freedom movement — Mahatma Gandhi and Lal Bahadur Shastri — were born on the same date (October 2), though 35 years apart. But the annals of history suggest that one’s ideas and ideals influenced the other immensely. On the birth anniversary of both leaders, we look at two critical junctures of Shastri’s life where Gandhi’s philosophy left a lasting impression, from his adolescent years in Varanasi all the way to his time as independent India’s second Prime Minister. In 1915, Gandhi arrived in India after his successful exploits in South Africa, where he transformed from a promising, young lawyer to a leading civil rights campaigner over the course of two decades (1893-1914). At the time, his focus on non-violent methods garnered much public attention. Shastri, only 11 at the time, was quite taken by Gandhi’s 1916 speech at the Banaras Hindu University (BHU). The prominent journalist D R Mankekar, in his book Builders of Modern India: Lal Bahadur Shastri (1973), wrote how Shastri could “never forget the day he first saw and heard the Mahatma”. items.text: Death row killer Christa Pike made final request before surviving botched execution
items.article: Death row killer Christa Pike made a final request before her execution in Tennessee - she survived the procedure despite two lethal injections Christa Pike, the death row inmate who survived two lethal injections this week, made an unusual final request prior to the botched execution. Pike , 50, was administered with two lethal injections in Tennessee’s death chamber but somehow survived. She was rushed to hospital shortly after and remains in a critical condition. She would have been the first woman the state put to death in 200 years. Her attorneys revealed yesterday that the convicted murderer requested no men be involved in administering the lethal drug. She made the request due to her history of suffering sexual abuse, fearing being put to death by a man would be needlessly traumatic. “That was her biggest fear as the victim of sexual abuse, that she would be pinned down, prodded, poked, cut,” one of her lawyers, Stephen Ferrell, said. “What I saw was consistent with that,” another of her lawyers, Randy Spivey, said in response to a question about whether the execution team had been staffed entirely by women. The botched injection saw Pike pinned down for around an hour as staff tried to set the two IV lines that would administer the lethal chemicals and supposedly end her life.

items.text: Meet Sudhakar Malli, RBI's new Executive Director
items.article: Malli is a career central banker with around three decades of experience, including more than two and a half decades in the supervision of banks, non-banking financial companies and co-operative banks. The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has appointed Sudhakar Malli as an Executive Director (ED), effective October 1, 2026, the bank said in a statement. He will succeed Suman Ray. Prior to his promotion, Malli was serving as Chief General Manager-in-Charge of the Department of Supervision at the central bank. Malli is a career central banker with around three decades of experience, including more than two and a half decades in the supervision of banks, non-banking financial companies ( NBFC s) and co-operative banks. Malli has extensive experience in financial-sector supervision, having worked across the supervision of banks, NBFCs and co-operative banks for over 25 years. He also has around five years of supervisory experience in overseas jurisdictions. In addition to his supervisory responsibilities, Malli has worked in the area of Currency Management during his career at the RBI . As Executive Director, Malli will oversee the Department of Supervision (Supervisory Assessment) at the RBI.
